title: What can you say about vitamin K in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for vitamin K; the strongest is "Supports normal blood clotting" (moderate, at least 11.25 µg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents or reverses artery calcification or heart disease".

supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review; Health Canada lists no specific use.
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: at least 11.25 µg, 15% of the 75 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). Health Canada's monograph gives vitamin K1 and K2 at 6-120 µg a day for adults but lists no specific use for it.
supported_wordings.form: Vitamin K1 or K2, counted as total vitamin K

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents or reverses artery calcification or heart disease

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
